patients.summary: Healthy college student from Easthampton who joined the practice at 18 with pollen allergies and acne. Between 2024 and 2026 he had three emergency admissions at a regional hospital for meningococcal-type bacterial meningitis, the last two with meningococcemia and low platelets, and recovered fully each time; the records that reach the practice are short ED notes and his own account.

documents.title: New Patient Inquiry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Gavin called, 18, lives in Easthampton with his family and heads to campus housing this month. His pediatrician's office told him he has aged out. Went over membership and how texting the doctor works; he is on the university student health plan, which we bill for labs and outside care. New patient appt booked 9/13 at 3:40 so it fits around his move-in. Asked him to sign the release for his pediatric records, sent through the portal.

conditions.label: Allergic rhinitis due to pollen
conditions.note: seasonal, spring worst; cetirizine as needed

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth daily as needed for allergy symptoms
Apply a thin layer to the face nightly

social.value: Campus dormitory during the school year; family home in Easthampton

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
18 y/o man here to set up adult primary care. Saw a pediatric group his whole life; records release signed, not here yet.

Concerns: none really. Mom wanted him to have a doctor near campus before the semester gets going.

PMH
- Seasonal allergies since middle school, spring is the bad stretch (sneezing, runny nose, itchy eyes). Cetirizine 10 mg when he needs it, over the counter. Some springs he takes it most days.
- Acne on the face since about 14. Uses adapalene gel at night, OTC. Happy enough with it, a few breakouts around exams.

PSH: tonsils out at 6. Wisdom teeth out at 17 with the oral surgeon, no problems.
Meds: cetirizine 10 mg PRN, adapalene 0.1% gel nightly.
Allergies: none to medications.
FH: father has high blood pressure. Paternal grandmother has rheumatoid arthritis. A cousin on his mother's side was hospitalized as a little kid with meningococcal infection and recovered; he does not know more than that.
SH: starting college, will be in a dorm on campus during the year and home in Easthampton on breaks. Never smoked, no vaping. Drinks socially on weekends, a few drinks at a party, denies blackouts or driving after drinking. No drugs. Single.

ROS negative except as above.

Exam: well-appearing, pleasant. Vitals as recorded. HEENT: nasal turbinates pink, no polyps; tonsillar fossae clear; TMs normal. Neck supple, no nodes. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Skin: a few closed comedones and two small papules on the forehead and chin, no cysts or scarring. Neuro grossly normal.

PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 2.

A/P
1. Allergic rhinitis, seasonal: fine on cetirizine as needed; start it a week or two before his usual spring flare.
2. Acne vulgaris, mild: continue adapalene nightly, pea-sized amount, moisturizer with SPF in the morning.
3. Health maintenance: one-time HIV and hepatitis C screening drawn today. Will check immunizations once pediatric records arrive; flu shot next month. Talked about alcohol and staying with friends at parties.
4. He gave permission for us to share health information with his mother; noted on the chart.

RTC for a physical next summer, or text anytime.

documents.title: Your Screening Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Gavin, both screening tests from Tuesday (HIV and hepatitis C) came back negative. These are once-in-adulthood screens, so nothing more to do unless something changes. Good luck with move-in.

documents.title: Pediatric Practice Records
documents.author: pediatrics
documents.body:
Records transfer, pediatric group, patient seen from infancy through age 18.

Summary of care: well-child visits yearly with normal growth and development. Tonsillectomy at age 6, uncomplicated. Seasonal allergic rhinitis from about age 11, managed with cetirizine. Acne vulgaris from about age 14, managed with topical adapalene. Third molars removed by oral surgery at 17. No hospitalizations otherwise. NKDA.

Immunizations: complete childhood series including MMR x2 and varicella x2. Tdap and MenACWY at the 11-year visit; HPV 9-valent x2 (11 and 11.5 years); MenACWY booster at 16; COVID-19 mRNA primary series 2021.

Last well visit at 17: normal exam, BMI in the normal range, vision and hearing screens passed.

documents.title: Outside Records Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Pediatric records reviewed. Matches what he told me. Vaccine history entered from their record. Due for flu this fall; nothing else outstanding.

documents.title: Nurse Visit: Flu Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Came by after class for his flu shot. No fever today, no prior reactions. Quadrivalent flu 0.5 mL IM left deltoid, lot and expiration on the immunization record. VIS given. Waited 15 minutes, fine, left.

documents.title: Allergies
documents.author: patient
documents.body: hi, my allergies are pretty bad this week, sneezing a ton and eyes itchy. i've been taking the cetirizine only some days. is it ok to take it every day?

documents.title: RE: Allergies
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, take it every day through the pollen season, usually into early June. It works better taken daily than chasing symptoms. If it makes you sleepy, take it at night. Any fever, facial pain or wheezing, let me know.

documents.title: School Form
documents.author: patient
documents.body: my school needs the health form and vaccine record updated for housing again this year. can I upload it here?

documents.title: RE: School Form
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Yes, attach it here. I printed your immunization record from our chart and the doctor will sign the form at your physical on 8/22. We'll upload the signed copy back to you that day.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. Turned 19 yesterday. Back to the dorm on the 30th.

Interval: good year. Allergies were rough in late April, did better once he took the cetirizine daily. Skin about the same, adapalene most nights.
Meds: cetirizine 10 mg daily in season / PRN otherwise; adapalene 0.1% gel nightly.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: dorm again. Drinks on some weekends, says 3-4 at most. No tobacco or vaping. Sleep okay. Mood fine.

PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 2.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Comfortable. Eyes, ears, throat normal. Neck no adenopathy. Heart RRR no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. Skin: scattered comedones on forehead, no inflammatory lesions to speak of. Normal gait and strength.

A/P
- Well adult.
- Allergic rhinitis: plan to start cetirizine daily mid-April next year.
- Acne: continue adapalene.
- Vaccines: up to date for now; flu and the new COVID shot when they come in this fall.
- College health form signed and returned to him through the portal.

Next physical summer 2024.

documents.title: Nurse Visit: Fall Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (quadrivalent) in the left arm and the 2023-24 COVID vaccine in the right, both IM, both tolerated. Screening questions negative. Told him a sore arm and feeling run-down for a day are common with the COVID shot. Observed 15 min, no issues.

documents.title: Skin
documents.author: patient
documents.body: my face has been breaking out more with midterms. should I put the adapalene on twice a day instead?

documents.title: RE: Skin
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Stick with once a night. Twice a day mostly just makes it red and peely without clearing faster. Give a flare 6 to 8 weeks to settle, wash with something gentle, and don't pick. If it is still bad by your physical we can talk about other options.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly visit. Home for part of the summer, back on campus in a few weeks.

Skin settled after the March flare; still on adapalene nightly. Allergy season okay this year on daily cetirizine April through May, now off it.
Meds: cetirizine PRN, adapalene 0.1% nightly. NKDA.
Social: dorm. Weekend drinking, a little more than last year he says, still no binges he can name, no driving. No tobacco or vapes.

PHQ-2 0, AUDIT-C 3.

Exam: well. Vitals ok. HEENT normal. Neck supple. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft. Skin: a few comedones on the forehead, no cysts. Neuro grossly normal.

A/P
- Healthy 19 y/o.
- Acne mild, controlled. Continue.
- Allergic rhinitis, seasonal, controlled.
- Alcohol: AUDIT-C under the cutoff; reviewed limits and not mixing with anything else.
- Fall vaccines when available. Physical next summer.

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 08/03/2024. Faxed to primary care 08/09/2024.

19M, college student, living in campus dorm. About 12 h of fever, bad headache and stiff neck. Says several friends in the dorm have been sick lately with something similar.
PMH: seasonal allergies, acne. PSH: tonsillectomy, wisdom teeth. Meds: cetirizine PRN, adapalene gel. Allergies: NKDA. Never smoker, social EtOH.

T 39.2 C, HR 110, BP 130/75.
Toxic-appearing, photophobic. Kernig and Brudzinski both positive. Petechiae across the trunk and both legs.

LP: CSF WBC 1200/mm3, 80% PMNs; glucose 20; protein 180. Gram stain with gram-negative diplococci.

Impression: meningococcal meningitis.
Ceftriaxone 2 g IV given in the ED. Droplet precautions. Admitted to medicine. Public health notified per protocol for contact tracing.

documents.title: Call From Patient's Mother
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mother called (on file as OK to share). Gavin went to the ED Saturday afternoon with fever, headache and stiff neck and was admitted; they told the family it is meningococcal meningitis and he is on IV antibiotics. She says he is more awake today and texting. Asked whether the family needs anything: the hospital and the health department are handling contacts, so follow their instructions. Asked her to have him message us when he is discharged so we can see him in the next week or two, and to have the hospital fax records. Will watch for them.

documents.title: Home
documents.author: patient
documents.body: hi, I got out of the hospital saturday. they said I'm done with antibiotics and I don't have any to take at home. mom said you wanted to see me?

documents.title: RE: Home
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad you're home. Yes, I'd like to see you next week. The front desk has you down for Tuesday the 20th at 10:20. Rest, drink plenty, and call or text right away for a new fever, worse headache, a rash, or if you feel confused.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after admission for meningococcal meningitis.

Got to the ED on 8/3 after about half a day of fever, headache and neck stiffness. ED note (faxed 8/9) shows LP with very high white count, low glucose, high protein and gram-negative diplococci. Per Gavin, about a week inpatient on IV antibiotics, home 8/10, nothing to take home. No discharge summary here yet.

Now: headache gone since the hospital. Tired, naps in the afternoon, getting better each day. No fever, neck pain, rash, vision changes, ringing or trouble hearing. Eating normally.
Meds: cetirizine PRN, adapalene. NKDA.

Exam: looks well. Afebrile. Alert, oriented, conversational. Skin clear, no petechiae or marks. Neck supple, full range. Heart regular, lungs clear. Cranial nerves intact, hears whispered voice both sides, strength and gait normal.

A/P
1. Meningococcal meningitis, treated inpatient, recovered. Fatigue expected for a few weeks. Back to normal activity as energy allows; ease in. CBC today.
2. Seasonal allergic rhinitis and acne, no changes.
Will keep asking for the hospital summary.

documents.title: Blood Count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your blood count from yesterday is completely normal: white cells, red cells and platelets all where they should be. Keep resting up, and reach out if anything changes.

documents.title: Nurse Visit: Fall Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for flu and 2024-25 COVID. Feeling well, no fever. Trivalent flu L deltoid, COVID R deltoid, IM. Lots on the record. Tolerated well, observed, left without problems.

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED. DOS 03/18/2025. Copy to PCP 03/28/2025.

20M, college student. Meningococcal meningitis 08/2024 (this hospital); also allergic rhinitis and acne. Roommate brought him in after spotting a rash on his arms and legs. Got home from a spring break trip two days ago; felt achy and run-down, which he put down to travel, then over the past few hours spiked a high fever with severe headache and could not bend his neck. Disoriented in triage, history limited, partly from roommate.
Meds: cetirizine PRN, adapalene gel. Allergies: NKDA. Never smoker; drinks socially, more on the recent trip per roommate.

T 39.2 C, BP 90/60, P 120, RR 22.
Petechiae with patches of purpura on the extremities. Nuchal rigidity, Brudzinski positive. Cap refill 3 s.

Labs: WBC 15.0, plt 100. Na 130, K 4.5, BUN 18, Cr 1.2. CRP 24 mg/L. Blood cultures sent, pending.
LP: CSF WBC 2000 with 90% PMNs, protein 150, glucose 20.

Impression: acute bacterial meningitis with meningococcemia; thrombocytopenia.
IV fluids. Ceftriaxone 2 g IV in the ED. Droplet precautions. Admitted to medicine.

documents.title: Call From Patient's Mother
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mother called early, upset. Gavin's roommate took him to the ED last night with fever, headache, a stiff neck and a rash; he was confused when he got there. Admitted again on IV antibiotics. Family drove over overnight. She asks whether this is the same thing as last summer; told her I don't know yet and the hospital team will know more once the tests are back. Asked her to keep us posted and that I'd see him after discharge. Requested ED and inpatient records.

documents.title: Out of the hospital again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: got discharged yesterday. was in about 8 days. they said my platelets were low at first but came back up before I left. no meds to take home. I'm at my parents' for a few days

documents.title: RE: Out of the hospital again
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know, and I'm sorry you went through that again. Let's see you in about 10 days with a blood count. Front desk will text you a time. Same warning signs as before: fever, headache, rash, confusion, call or text right away, day or night.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after his second meningitis admission.

ED 3/18, two days after coming back from a spring break trip: fever, headache, stiff neck, rash with purpura, low BP, confused. ED note (received 3/28): WBC 15, platelets 100, Na 130, Cr 1.2, CRP 24; CSF WBC 2000, 90% PMNs, protein 150, glucose 20; blood cultures pending at the time. Treated as bacterial meningitis with meningococcemia. He says about 8 days inpatient on IV antibiotics, platelets recovered before discharge on 3/26, nothing to take home. No discharge summary or culture result has come to us.

Now: back in classes this week, tired by evening but improving. No headache, fever or neck pain. Rash faded over the first week home. Hearing fine. Thinking clearly, catching up on coursework.
Meds: cetirizine PRN, adapalene. NKDA.
Social: drank more than usual on the spring break trip, back to weekends only.

Exam: well-appearing. Afebrile, BP normal. Skin: no petechiae, purpura or scarring on the arms or legs. Neck supple. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Alert and oriented, cranial nerves intact, strength and gait normal.

A/P
1. Acute bacterial meningitis with meningococcemia and thrombocytopenia, recovered. CBC and BMP today to make sure platelets, sodium and creatinine are back to normal.
2. Allergy season coming: start cetirizine daily.
3. Acne: continue adapalene.
Physical in July.

documents.title: Your Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news: platelets, white count and hemoglobin are all normal, and so are your sodium and kidney function. Nothing more to check for now.

documents.title: Missed Physical
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called about yesterday's missed 9:00 physical. He apologized, had the date wrong. Rebooked for Tuesday 7/29 at 8:20. Reminder text set for the day before.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, rescheduled from 7/8.

Since April: feels back to normal, finished the semester. No fevers, headaches or rashes. Allergies were manageable on daily cetirizine in spring. Skin okay on adapalene.
History: meningitis admissions 8/2024 and 3/2025, recovered from both.
Meds: cetirizine PRN, adapalene 0.1% nightly. NKDA.
Social: dorm again in the fall. Alcohol on weekends; he volunteers that the spring break trip was the heaviest drinking he has done and that it scared him a little after what followed. No tobacco or vaping.

PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 3.

Exam: vitals fine. HEENT normal. Neck supple, no nodes. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Skin: occasional comedones, no lesions on the extremities. Neuro normal.

A/P
- Healthy 20 y/o, recovered from two meningitis admissions.
- Tdap today; last one at 11 per pediatric record.
- Alcohol: under the screening cutoff; talked through pacing and keeping an eye on friends.
- Rhinitis and acne stable on current regimen.
- Flu shot in the fall.

documents.title: Nurse Visit: Flu Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine, trivalent, 0.5 mL IM right deltoid. Feels well. Declined COVID this year, says he'll think about it. Tolerated, observed 15 min.

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Service date 01/31/2026. Sent to PCP on request 02/24/2026.

21M with seasonal allergies and acne, two prior admissions here for bacterial meningitis (8/2024, 3/2025). Two days of fever, headache and neck stiffness. Rash he describes as not itchy, first on his trunk and now on his arms and legs. Roommate was diagnosed with bacterial meningitis recently.
Meds: cetirizine as needed, adapalene. NKDA.

T 39.2 C, HR 110, BP 90/60.
Petechial rash, coalescing into purpura in areas. Nuchal rigidity.

WBC 15.0, Hgb 13.5, plt 50.
PT 18 s (ref 11-13.5), PTT 45 s (ref 25-35), fibrinogen 150 mg/dL (ref 200-400).

Impression: meningococcemia with thrombocytopenia and prolonged clotting times; clinical bacterial meningitis.
LP deferred given platelets and coags. Ceftriaxone 2 g IV given. Fluids. Droplet precautions. Admitted to medicine.

documents.title: Call From Patient's Mother
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mother called. Gavin was admitted Saturday, same hospital, fever and rash again. She says his roommate had meningitis a couple of weeks ago. He is on IV antibiotics and they told her his platelets are low. Talking and eating some as of last night. Told her I'd like to see him within a week or two of getting home and asked her to have him text me when he's out. Requested records again.

documents.title: discharged
documents.author: patient
documents.body: home since yesterday, they kept me 9 days this time. done with the IV antibiotics, nothing to take. really tired

documents.title: RE: discharged
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad you're out. Tired is expected for a while. I have you Tuesday 2/17 at 1:20, and we'll check your blood count and clotting labs. Text me any time before then if the fever, headache or rash come back.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Third admission. Seen one week after discharge.

Per Gavin and his mother's call: ED 1/31 after two days of fever, headache, stiff neck and a spreading rash; roommate had bacterial meningitis shortly before. Told his platelets and clotting were off and they did not do a spinal tap. About 9 days of IV antibiotics, home 2/9, no antibiotic after. We still have no ED note or discharge summary; front desk sending another request today.

Now: tired, sleeping a lot, slowly better. No headache, fever, neck pain, bleeding or bruising. Rash has faded. Hearing and vision normal. Plans to go back to class next week.
Meds: cetirizine PRN, adapalene. NKDA.

Exam: well-appearing. Afebrile, vitals normal. Skin: no petechiae, purpura or scarring. Neck supple. Heart regular, lungs clear. Alert, oriented, cranial nerves intact, strength and gait normal.

A/P
1. Meningococcemia with thrombocytopenia and clinical bacterial meningitis, treated, recovering. CBC and PT/INR today.
2. Return to class as tolerated.
3. Allergic rhinitis and acne unchanged.
Follow up by message with results.

documents.title: Records Request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Faxed a records request to the regional hospital's health information department for the 1/31/2026 ED visit and the admission (ED note, discharge summary, labs). Second request; first was called in 2/2.
